_about: Stock collection cup and its joint to the cone, measured from photos and video frames (issue 269). Lengths in mm. pm = +- uncertainty (about 1 sigma, judgement included). confidence: high / medium / low / not_determined. measure.py reproduces every number marked method=fit or method=read.

_sources.k0: 4K photo image-1795800846956-0.jpg (issue 269, Nov 17): top flange face with the centring ring removed
_sources.k1: 4K photo image-1795800846973-1.jpg (issue 269, Nov 17): cracked glass, guard, bottom plate with tie rods, 18 mm wrench
_sources.p04: WhatsApp photo 04 (Nov 16): cup top with the KF centring ring and O-ring in place
_sources.p09: WhatsApp photo 09 (Nov 17): AMAZEMET's metal cup on another machine

type.value: ISO-KF (ISO 2861): centring ring with O-ring, hinged two-segment clamp with wing nut
type.method: visual: metal centring ring inside a brown (FKM-coloured) O-ring on a flat face; with the ring off, the face is flat with a counterbore step at the bore and no gasket groove (a tri-clamp ferrule has a bead groove and a flat gasket, no metal ring)

size.method: ellipse fits: O-ring OD / flange OD = 0.827 (rms < 1 px); nominal KF-50 0.867, ISO-K 63 0.901, KF-40 0.945, KF-25 0.950. Training video calls the stack's flange 'K50'.

flange_od.method: standard size of the identified flange; cross-check: if the O-ring is the standard 55 x 5 (OD 65), the fits give 78.6, so check with calipers

centring_ring_bore_seen.method: fit ratio 0.585 x 75; smaller than the ~50 mm bore of common KF-50 rings, so either a reduced-bore ring or the edge found is deeper in the bore

clamp.value: hinged KF clamp, wing nut, finger-tightened
clamp.source: t6_0040 (clamp on the mat), t4_545 (on the joint); training video 5 at 4:48 'just finger tightening for the flange'

z_joint_face_above_mat.method: no frame shows the mounted cup side-on with the floor at a known scale; 300 is the Oct 2026 viz3d estimate from 720p frames

cup_hangs_on_clamp.method: the cup stays on the cone when the cone swings out; the trainer says to lift the container and clamp it at the same time

drop_to_unclamp.value: a few mm to clear the centring ring's lips, then slide sideways

stack_top_to_bottom: conical reducer (KF-50 up to the valve body)
sanitary butterfly valve, two bolted halves, EPDM seat, lever with ball knob on a side hub
glass tube in a perforated guard, 4 tie rods
bottom plate with the glass seal groove and a shallow pocket

overall_height.method: sum of parts: KF face to valve flange 53 (measured, low) + valve body ~50 + top plate ~12 + glass gap ~100 + bottom plate ~6; not measured directly

bottom_plate_od.reference: 18 mm wrench box end (154 px -> 8.4 px/mm) and tie-rod shank if 12 mm (107 px -> 8.9 px/mm), mean 8.67 px/mm
bottom_plate_od.method: RANSAC ellipse fit of the plate's top edge, major axis 1478 px (rms 1.6 px)

bottom_plate_rim_t.method: chamfer + side band at the front, 32 px, divided by sin(38 deg view tilt)

top_plate_od.method: looks the same as the bottom plate in t5_0034 and t6_0040

glass_od.method: silhouette width at the table (859 px) over the plate's major axis, 3 % depth correction; bracketed by the gasket band 92-107

glass_wall.method: rim seen edge-on at its left extreme (64 px) over the rim's width (1078 px)

glass_len.method: k1 rim ellipses give ~98 (weak-perspective model, top rim 25 % nearer the camera); t6 side view gives guard height 0.70 x plate OD ~ 120

glass_seal_band_od.method: outer edge of the black gasket band, 931 px over the plate's 1478 px

glass_seal_band_id.method: inner edge of the band, 794 px; the gasket is lifted and twisted, so the groove itself may differ

tie_rods.method: rod shank 107 px at the wrench scale; nut silhouette / rod = 1.63 (ISO M12 nut 18 AF: AF/d 1.50, AC/d 1.73); an 18 mm wrench lay with the parts; smooth rods with threaded ends, plain hex nuts on the bottom plate, acorn nuts on top

tie_rod_bolt_circle.method: each nut's outer face sits 2-5 mm inside the plate rim: 170.5 - 2 x (9.3 + 3.5)

guard_od.method: 0.68 x plate width in a low side view

mass_estimate_kg.method: plates, valve, reducer, glass and rods by volume

kf_face_to_valve_flange_top.method: centre-to-centre image offset of the KF face and the 4-bolt valve flange over sin(67 deg) view tilt, mean scale with a 7 % depth correction

reducer_large_end_od.method: 390 px vs the flange's 472 px, 5 % depth correction; fits 2.5 in (63.5 mm) tube, so likely a 2 in to 2.5 in reducer and a DN65-class valve

valve_body_flange_od.method: 650 px vs 472 px, 7 % depth correction; 4 bolts with acorn nuts

type.value: sanitary butterfly valve with an EPDM seat ring; lever with a black ball knob on a cylindrical side hub; body halves bolted with acorn nuts
type.source: p04, k0, t5_0034, t6_0040, t4_545; AMAZEMET: 'the rubber that is around the valve part', EPDM

bore.method: inferred from the reducer's ~65 mm large end (2.5 in tube); not seen directly

splash_plate.value: curved stainless strip/plate across about half the bore below the valve seat, a semicircular notch near each end
splash_plate.method: visual only; strong perspective and unknown depth, so no size

cone_shields.value: thin round discs laid in the mouth of the swing-out cone; splashes stick to them and the powder falls past; one for aluminium, more for hot metals such as copper
cone_shields.confidence: low for size, high for what and where

amazemet_metal_cup.value: plain stainless tube hung from the cone outlet with hinged sanitary clamps; a lever (ball knob) butterfly valve on a side branch below the outlet; a second valve and clamp mid-height; the tube runs down to near the floor of the frame
amazemet_metal_cup.source: p09; training video 5 at 0:00-0:35 'a very simple tube and the valve is added separately'
